questions.stem: What is the definition of acceleration?

options.text: The rate of change of velocity
The rate of change of distance
The total distance travelled per unit time

questions.explanation: Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity. It tells you how quickly the velocity is changing.

questions.stem: What is the SI unit of acceleration?
questions.explanation: The SI unit of acceleration is metres per second squared (m/s^2), meaning velocity changes by that many m/s every second.

questions.stem: A car accelerates from rest to 20 m/s in 5 seconds. What is its acceleration?
An object is moving at constant velocity. What is its acceleration?
questions.explanation: If velocity is constant (not changing), the rate of change of velocity is zero, so the acceleration is zero.

options.text: An object that is speeding up
An object moving backwards at constant speed
An object that is slowing down

questions.explanation: Negative acceleration (deceleration) means the velocity is decreasing in magnitude -- the object is slowing down.

questions.stem: Which equation correctly relates final velocity (v), initial velocity (u), acceleration (a), and time (t)?
questions.explanation: The equation v = u + at comes directly from rearranging the definition of acceleration: a = (v - u) / t.

questions.stem: An acceleration of 3 m/s^2 means that every second, the velocity increases by:
questions.explanation: An acceleration of 3 m/s^2 means the velocity increases by 3 metres per second every second.
